title: Ghana Macroeconomic Dashboard
text:
Ghana’s economy sits at a fascinating intersection of colonial history, commodity dependence, and recurring IMF intervention. This project explores how key macroeconomic indicators — GDP, inflation, interest rates, exchange rates, and commodity prices — have evolved since independence, and what their relationships reveal about the structural dynamics of a developing economy.
The final product is an interactive Shiny dashboard that allows users to explore these indicators visually and run their own Granger Causality tests to investigate lead-lag relationships between variables.
Tools used: R, Shiny, ggplot2, Ghana Statistical Service, Bank of Ghana data

title: Ghana Macroeconomic Dashboard
text:
Key Question

Ghana has relied on IMF bailouts in 1966, the 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, 2009, 2015, and 2022. Each intervention coincides with periods of currency depreciation, rising inflation, and commodity price shocks. But do these patterns follow conventional economic theory — or does Ghana’s developing economy behave differently?

title: Ghana Macroeconomic Dashboard
text:
Data & Methodology
Data was sourced from the Ghana Statistical Service and the Bank of Ghana, arriving in inconsistent monthly formats across multiple Excel files. A custom R cleaning pipeline standardized date formats, removed formatting artifacts, handled missing values, and converted all monthly series into annual averages. Year-over-year (YoY) transformations were calculated for key variables including inflation, exchange rates, gold prices, GDP, monetary supply, cocoa prices, and oil prices — because YoY changes highlight turning points and accelerations that raw levels obscure.
Granger Causality was chosen over standard regression because the core economic questions involve lead-lag relationships: does inflation predict future policy rate decisions? Do commodity prices lead exchange rate movements? Granger testing is specifically designed to answer these questions.

title: Ghana Macroeconomic Dashboard
text:
Key Findings
Inflation and monetary policy move together, with a lag. During periods of economic stress (2009, 2015, 2022), inflation spiked and the Bank of Ghana responded by raising its policy rate — which in turn pushed up commercial lending rates. The dashboard makes this lagged relationship visible and testable.
Cocoa and the cedi are linked — but gold is different. When the cedi depreciates, Ghanaian farmers earn more cedis per dollar exported, incentivizing oversupply on the world market and pushing cocoa prices down. Gold, however, behaves as global money driven by US dollar strength, geopolitical risk, and global inflation expectations — not Ghanaian supply dynamics. A Granger Causality test on gold prices vs. the cedi returned a p-value of 0.1757, indicating gold does not show clear predictive power for the cedi once its own past is controlled for.
IMF interventions are visible but hard to isolate. The 2009, 2015, and 2022 bailout periods all coincide with currency instability and rising inflation, but isolating the precise effect of each program is difficult given the extended duration of interventions and the confounding effects of global commodity shocks.

title: Ghana Macroeconomic Dashboard
text:
Reflection
This project reinforced that macroeconomic relationships in developing economies rarely follow textbook predictions cleanly. Ghana’s heavy dependence on gold, cocoa, and oil exposes it to global price shocks outside its control, while recurring IMF engagement reflects structural challenges that short-term stabilization programs cannot fully resolve. Future extensions would incorporate higher-frequency monthly or weekly data to capture short-run dynamics that annual averages smooth out.

title: Netflix Shows And Movies Analysis
text:
Netflix began as a DVD rental service and evolved into the world’s largest streaming platform. This analysis explores how Netflix’s content library has changed between 2008 and 2021, specifically how the balance between movies and TV shows has shifted, how rapidly the platform scaled its catalogue, and which genres drove that growth. Understanding these trends reveals the strategic decisions Netflix made to dominate the streaming wars and retain subscribers in an increasingly competitive market.
Key question: How has Netflix’s content strategy evolved over time, and what does that tell us about how the platform competes?









The first plot, “Proportion of TV Shows and Movies by Year”, shows the proportion of TV shows and movies added to Netflix each year. This is a stacked bar chart, where each year is represented by a bar, with segments showing the proportion of TV shows and movies.In the graph, movies tended to dominate the viewing options especially from 2009 to 2012. Although TV Shows in 2008 had the same as movies. In recent years however,the proportion of TV shows have increased with about 25 percent of viewing options being TV shows.









The second plot, “Trend of TV Shows and Movies Added by Year”, shows the actual counts of TV shows and movies added per year. This is a line plot with different colors representing movies and TV shows. Between 2015 and 2020, they both experienced steep growths however movies added far outweighed TV Shows added









The third plot, “Variations in Number of Movies and TV Shows by Genre and Year”, shows how different genres have varied over the years with respect to both TV Shows and Movies. In recent years, there’s been growth in all the genres, however Comedies, Dramas, Documentary and Action movies rose more highly. Although Crimes, Kid’s TV and Romantic movies have all risen in the TV Shows category, they are still below that of movies.

title: Netflix Shows And Movies Analysis
text:
Conclusion
Taken together, these three analyses tell a clear story: Netflix deliberately transformed itself from a movie-first platform into a broad content powerhouse. In its early years, movies made up the vast majority of the catalogue, but from 2015 onward, Netflix aggressively expanded both volume and variety. The surge in TV shows is particularly telling; series keep subscribers engaged month after month in a way that films cannot. Meanwhile, the genre breakdown reveals that this wasn’t random growth, Dramas, Comedies, and Documentaries led the expansion, reflecting Netflix’s bet on prestige content that attracts awards attention and cultural conversation. The data suggests Netflix’s content strategy has always been intentional, data-driven, and evolving.

title: Premier League Match Analysis
text:
The Premier League is widely regarded as the most competitive domestic football league in the world, where fine margins separate the top of the table from the bottom. This analysis explores match-level data from the 2021/22 Premier League season to understand what actually drives goals and match outcomes. Specifically, it investigates three questions: Does shooting more lead to scoring more? Does shot accuracy matter more than shot volume? And does playing at home provide a measurable scoring advantage?
Key question: What factors are most associated with scoring goals in the Premier League, and how much of an edge does home advantage really provide?

title: Premier League Match Analysis
text:

This analysis explores match-level data from the 2021/22 Premier League season to understand what actually drives goals and match outcomes. Specifically, it investigates three questions: Does shooting more lead to scoring more? Does shot accuracy matter more than shot volume? And does playing at home provide a measurable scoring advantage?
Key question: What factors are most associated with scoring goals in the Premier League, and how much of an edge does home advantage really provide?

title: Premier League Match Analysis
text:
Shots vs. Goals









The scatter plot above shows the relationship between the number of shots a home team takes and the number of goals they score in a match. The trend line shows a positive relationship — teams that take more shots tend to score more goals — but the relationship is far from perfect. Many matches with 15-20 shots still resulted in zero or one goal, while a handful of matches saw teams convert relatively few shots into multiple goals. This suggests that shot volume alone is not the full story behind scoring output.

title: Premier League Match Analysis
text:
Shot Accuracy vs. Goals









This second plot narrows the focus from total shots to shots on target, a more direct measure of attacking quality. The relationship here is noticeably tighter than the first plot, suggesting that shot accuracy is a stronger predictor of goals than shot volume alone. In other words, teams that consistently test the goalkeeper are more likely to score than teams that simply shoot often without precision. This points to a broader insight: quality of chances created often matters more than raw shot count.

title: Premier League Match Analysis
text:
Home Advantage









The final chart compares the average number of goals scored by home teams versus away teams across the entire season. Home teams scored more goals on average than away teams, confirming the long-discussed “home advantage” effect in football. This is likely driven by a combination of factors not captured in this dataset, including crowd support, travel fatigue for the away side, and greater familiarity with the pitch and surroundings.

title: Premier League Match Analysis
text:
Conclusion
Taken together, these three analyses suggest that goals in the Premier League are driven less by sheer shot volume and more by shot quality and contextual factors like home advantage. While teams that take more shots do tend to score more, the relationship strengthens considerably when looking specifically at shots on target, indicating that precision matters more than persistence. Additionally, the consistent home scoring advantage reinforces why managers and analysts place so much emphasis on home form when evaluating a team’s title or relegation chances. Ultimately, the data tells a clear story: in the Premier League, quality of opportunity and home support are just as important as the raw number of attempts a team generates.
